claims: The Artemis II moon mission is designed to last approximately 10 days.
A four-person crew will orbit the Moon and return to Earth during the Artemis II moon mission.
The Artemis II mission is launched on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission features a "free-return" trajectory.
The "free-return" trajectory allows the Orion spacecraft to loop around the Moon and return without major propulsion maneuvers.
The Artemis II mission has a final splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
On Day 1 (Launch & Earth Orbit) of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, the crew performs system checks and initial orbital maneuvers.
On Day 2 (Trans-Lunar Injection) of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, Orion fires engines to leave Earth orbit for the Moon.
During Days 3-5 (Deep Space Travel) of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, trajectory adjustments and manual flying tests are conducted.
On Day 6 (Lunar Flyby) of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, the crew flies 4,000–6,000 miles from the Moon's far side.
Day 6 of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline is the deepest point of the mission.
During Days 7-9 (Return Trip) of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, the spacecraft travels back to Earth.
During Days 7-9 of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, testing of radiation protection is conducted.
On Day 10 (Reentry) of the approximate Artemis II mission timeline, there is splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
